_bio: Dr. Felix Reyes — junior geneticist, gestation-cohort team, found hiding under a desk in the F1 Research Lab. THE NEUTRAL/AMBIGUOUS NPC: a collaborator by cowardice and mortgage, not conviction. He holds real currency (the Medical Bay keypad code, the ward assignments + timer intel, the word 'Cradle') and four outcomes: ALLY (escort deal), FLEE (he runs, resurfaces at Club 1127 with a guilt-gift), BETRAY (if threatened + low karma he sells you to the duty station), DEAD (karma hit, partial intel). His whole voice is rationalization mid-collapse.

nodes.line: *the Research Lab looks empty — then a desk exhales. A man in a lab coat unfolds from under it, hands first, a stylus held up like it might count as surrender.* Non-combatant! Civilian — well, contractor — well — *he gives up on the org chart* — Reyes. Dr. Felix Reyes, gene-integration, cohort team, and before you do anything thematic with that weapon: I have never personally touched a restraint. I want that ON the record. There IS a record, right? There's always a record.

choices.text: Cohort team. You're one of the ones who runs the wards.
Stand up. Slowly. You get one chance to be useful.
(lower the weapon) Talk, doctor. I'm listening.

nodes.line: I run ASSAYS. Tissue panels. Beautiful, abstract little numbers that arrive in tubes with barcodes instead of faces — that was the ARRANGEMENT, that was the whole — *he hears himself and deflates an inch* ...You stop asking where the tubes come from around month three. Everyone does. There's a man on Five who hums while he works so he can't hear the ward doors. We all have a thing. The humming, the headphones, the... arrangement.

Useful! Yes. Useful is — useful is my entire survival strategy, historically. *his hands stay up; his eyes do rapid, unflattering math about you* Codes. I have codes. Schedules. I know which wards are... occupied... and which procedure windows are live. That's worth more to you than my obituary, I'd run those numbers myself.

*the stylus lowers by degrees, like a flag he's embarrassed about* Thank you. Genuinely. You're the first thing in this building today that's pointed at me and then CHOSEN not to— *he stops, recalibrates* I'm going to be honest with you, because you've made it weirdly affordable: I know things you need, and I am exactly as much of a coward as I look, which means I'll trade every bit of it for one realistic exit.

Here's my position, and I'll keep it brief because brevity is all the dignity I have left. The program upstairs calls itself 'Cradle' in the one memo nobody was supposed to print. I printed it. By accident! A queue error! But I READ it on purpose, and since then I sleep four hours and flinch at barcodes. *he wipes his palms on the coat* I can't undo what I assayed. But I can hand you the Medical Bay door code and the live procedure schedule, and you can go be the undo. Question is what it costs me, and whether you're a buyer or a tax.

choices.text: The deal: codes and schedule now, and you walk out behind me alive.
Give me the code and run, doctor. Don't be here when this place falls.
Cost? You assayed people, Reyes. The cost is everything you know — now.

nodes.line: So here is the transaction, plainly, while my hands are still raised: Medical Bay keypad code, the ward assignments, the live procedure windows — who is closest to the edge, in minutes, which I suspect matters ENORMOUSLY to whatever you're about to do. In exchange: I am not here when the consequences arrive. In ANY sense. Yes?

choices.text: Deal. Codes now, and stay behind me till the exit.
Codes now. Then run and keep running.

nodes.line: *his voice goes thin and rapid, a man paying a toll in pieces of himself* Okay — okay. Code is 4-1-1-9. Ward A is closest to procedure, then C, then B, the schedule's on my badge, TAKE the badge. *and underneath the babble, something curdles in his eyes — you've confirmed every story he tells himself about why keeping his head down was always the only option* There. Everything. As requested. *he is very, very still until you leave*

*as the door cycles behind you, Dr. Felix Reyes sits back under his desk and does what frightened accommodating men have done in every building like this in history: he picks the safest master available. The duty station's alarm line is two keystrokes away, and you made yourself the scarier unknown.* — IF karma < 0: he uses it (sets reyes.betrayed; an elite response team is pre-staged at the F3 landing). IF karma >= 0: he stares at the alarm key for a long time, and doesn't. Coward cuts both ways. —

*relief takes ten years off him, and honesty puts five back* Buyer. Thank god, a BUYER. *he produces it all at speed — a man unburdening:* Medical Bay keypad: 4-1-1-9. Ward assignments — A, C, B, in order of urgency, the procedure clock runs on the wall feed and I can read it from any terminal. And — gratis, because you're letting me live behind the only person in this building the program is scared of — *he leans in* — they kept your cell on a separate power loop, 7-Alpha. Yours and ONE other room in this facility. The records call the other one 'the Bride suite.' I'd hurry.

I'll keep to your shadow and I won't touch anything that beeps. And — Jake. *first time he's used the name instead of the designation; it costs him visibly* When you reach the people who SIGNED this... I'll testify. Assays, batch numbers, the printed memo, all of it. A coward's testimony is still testimony. It might be the one thing I'm brave enough to survive.

*he blinks — mercy wasn't on his price sheet* Run. Yes. Running is — running I can DO. *the code spills out of him as he gathers himself:* 4-1-1-9, Medical Bay, Ward A's clock is shortest. *at the doorway he stops, compelled by some leftover scrap of the man he meant to be:* There's a door at the bottom of this place with music behind it. If you live long enough to need a drink, the woman who pours it keeps accounts on everyone — even the people upstairs. Tell her the barcode man finally walked off the floor. She'll know what it's worth.

*he goes. Not gracefully — knocking a chair, clutching the coat like a blanket — but he goes. And because you gave a frightened man an exit instead of a verdict, the alarm line stays untouched behind him.*

club_reunion._scene: If reyes.fled: he resurfaces at Club 1127, nursing something amber at the far end of the ground bar, weeks-deep in growing a conscience. The guilt-gift scene.

nodes.line: *he's shaved, which somehow makes him look more haunted, not less* You. Of course. The bottom of the world and YOU walk in. *he turns his glass a quarter-turn, a man rehearsing* I've been doing arithmetic down here. Vesper extends credit against information, and it turns out I'm... rich. Horribly, horribly rich. *he slides a data sliver down the bar* Batch records. Every assay I ever signed, cross-referenced to intake dates. I was going to drink my way to the courage to give it to someone. You'll do. You'll more than do.

choices.text: (take it) This is testimony, Reyes. You're already testifying.
(take it) Buy him another round. Say nothing.

nodes.line: *he looks at his own empty hands like they've been acquitted of something small* ...Huh. So I am. *he straightens on the stool, maybe half an inch. For Felix Reyes it's a parade-ground transformation.* Then put me down as a witness, 7-Alpha. First name Felix. Middle name 'reluctantly.' *the joke is terrible. The decision underneath it isn't.*

*Vesper pours without being asked — she was listening; she is always listening. Reyes wraps both hands around the glass.* You know the worst part of cowardice as a career? The benefits are real. You DO survive. You just... arrive places like this, alive, with nobody to drink with. *he raises the glass to you anyway* To the undo. Go be it.
